title: RG Veda
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: CLAMP's debut epic, loosely drawn from Indian mythology. The thunder god Taishakuten has overthrown the king of the gods and rules harshly; Yasha, the lord of a clan sent to kill a prophesied child, spares that child, Ashura, instead. After Yasha's people are destroyed, he and Ashura travel to gather the Six Stars foretold to end Taishakuten's reign.
life_message: Love and loyalty to those you protect are worth keeping even against a destiny written in blood.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Yasha's revenge for his slaughtered clan and personal loyalty drive the plot.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Heroes defy the established heavenly order to overthrow its ruler.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Clan identity and a found family matter more than the realm at large.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Kings, clans and royal lines; Ashura's royal heritage.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Prophecy, gods and destiny guide everything.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival in a war against a tyrant dominates.

folkways.japan: CLAMP reworks Hindu and Buddhist figures familiar in Japan through Buddhist art (such as Ashura and Yasha guardians), a common Japanese way of borrowing myth.

delivery.evidence: Otaku USA calls it fast-paced and action-heavy and raises no preachiness; theme carried by the quest (to verify).
delivery.note: The themes of fate and rebellion are carried by the quest and its losses rather than stated as lessons.

winners_losers: Sympathy lies with Yasha, Ashura and the Six Stars resisting Taishakuten; tags point to a tragic ending in which fate exacts a heavy price.
